title: Zephyrine and the Veil
premise: In the walled city of Vantrelle, where magic is outlawed and memories are currency, Elodie Joubert survives by stealing small recollections—first kisses, dead mothers' voices—and selling them as charms. When the border wards collapse on the night every star vanishes, she learns her own stolen childhood memory was the keystone that held them, sold years ago by the man who raised her to the court beneath the mountain, where a dying dragon-fire is fed with souls. To restore the wards and relight the stars, Elodie must descend into the Undercourt, outwit its soul-broker queen, and steal back not only her memory but the soul of the fire's last keeper—a boy she once loved and betrayed. She succeeds only by surrendering her talent forever, choosing an ordinary, belonging life in a city that finally remembers what it outlawed.
about_author: Elodie Vasquez is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters in a colonial records office before turning to fiction. She writes about thieves, borders, and the things people sell to survive, and lives near the sea with an opinionated cat.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Light
chapters.summary: Elodie lifts a widow's grief from a pawnshop ledger and sells it before curfew, establishing her rules: never take from the desperate, never be seen. POV Elodie. Emotional beat: lonely competence—the charm of her trade shadowed by how much of herself she has already sold.

chapters.title: Curfew Bells
chapters.summary: A wardens' sweep forces Elodie to shelter with Maren, a fence who keeps illegal maps, and we learn seven years ago Elodie arrived at the walls with no memories at all. POV Elodie. Emotional beat: unease; her blank past itches like a scar she can't stop touching.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Every star above Vantrelle gutters dark; the border wards fall with a sound like breaking glass. Panic floods the streets, and wardens begin conscripting anyone with 'talent.' POV Elodie. Emotional beat: terror and a strange, guilty exhilaration—invisibility is over whether she likes it or not.

chapters.title: What the Warden Knew
chapters.summary: Warden-Captain Ilsa Reyne catches Elodie mid-escape but doesn't arrest her; instead she reveals the wards were keyed to a stolen memory and offers freedom for cooperation. POV Ilsa. Emotional beat: cold pragmatism masking a warden's fear that the law she serves was built on theft.

chapters.title: The Man Who Raised a Thief
chapters.summary: Elodie confronts Corvin, her foster-father and fellow thief, who confesses he sold her childhood memory to a broker to pay a debt—one night of stars for one night of survival. POV Elodie. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallizing into purpose; rage with nowhere legal to go.

chapters.title: Charms for the Drowning
chapters.summary: As refugees press against the fallen wards, Elodie sells comfort-memories cheaply and witnesses what people will pay to feel safe. POV Elodie. Emotional beat: tenderness sharpening into resolve—her stolen goods are the only mercy left in the city.

chapters.title: The Broker's Card
chapters.summary: Following Corvin's clue, Elodie finds the broker's calling card stitched inside a stolen shawl: a dragon sigil, and an invitation written in her own seven-year-old handwriting. POV Elodie. Emotional beat: dread—the Undercourt has been expecting her all along.

chapters.title: Down the Stair That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Guided by Maren's maps and Ilsa's blind eye, Elodie enters the passage beneath the mountain, where stairs rearrange themselves and the dark remembers names. POV Elodie. Emotional beat: claustrophobic courage; each step costs a small memory as toll.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Elodie reaches the Undercourt, a cathedral of bone-lanterns lit by the guttering last dragon-fire, where the soul-broker Queen Sarelle holds court over the traded dead. POV Elodie. Emotional beat: awful beauty—she recognizes the architecture of her own stolen childhood.

chapters.title: A Boy Made of Ember
chapters.summary: Among the fire's keepers Elodie finds Tomas—the boy she betrayed at fourteen, now half-consumed, his soul the wick keeping the dragon-fire alive. POV Tomas. Emotional beat: heartbreak and fury; he remembers everything she paid to forget.

chapters.title: The Price of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Queen Sarelle offers a bargain: the city's wards restored if Elodie takes Tomas's place as keeper. POV Sarelle. Emotional beat: seductive despair—the queen genuinely believes someone must burn so others may belong.

chapters.title: Seven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Regaining fragments through the fire, Elodie relives the memory she lost: it was she who first sold Tomas's name to save herself, and Corvin merely completed the transaction. POV Elodie. Emotional beat: devastating self-recognition; she is not the victim of the story.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Steals Herself
chapters.summary: Refusing both bargains, Elodie begins stealing back pieces of the court itself—a guard's loyalty, a lantern's hunger—learning the limits of her gift. POV Elodie. Emotional beat: defiant ingenuity; thieving turned into resistance.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Door
chapters.summary: Above, Ilsa defies her superiors to hold the mountain pass open, buying Elodie time as conscription riots tear Vantrelle apart. POV Ilsa. Emotional beat: costly loyalty—the lawbreaker becomes the law's best servant.

chapters.title: Corvin Descends
chapters.summary: Corvin arrives to sell the queen one final memory—Elodie's location—but instead burns his own hoarded decades to buy her an hour. POV Corvin. Emotional beat: ragged redemption; love arriving too late to be simple.

chapters.title: The Queen's Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Elodie discovers Sarelle's secret: the queen sold her own soul centuries ago and rules as a hollow thing sustained by the fire. POV Elodie. Emotional beat: pity displacing hatred—the enemy is also a survivor paying a price.

chapters.title: Stealing Fire
chapters.summary: The climax begins: Elodie steals the dragon-fire itself—not the flame but the memory of warmth it feeds on—while Tomas's soul unravels in her hands. POV Elodie. Emotional beat: desperate audacity; the greatest theft of her life.

chapters.title: What the Fire Remembers
chapters.summary: Sarelle collapses as her sustaining memory is taken; in her last lucid moment she releases the court's souls, including Tomas, and asks only to be forgotten kindly. POV Sarelle. Emotional beat: release—an antagonist granted dignity and peace.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Tomas, freed but fading, chooses to carry the fire's memory up the mountain himself rather than let it die, asking Elodie to remember him honestly this time. POV Tomas. Emotional beat: sacrificial hope transformed—he gives the flame willingly instead of being consumed.

chapters.title: Stars Over Vantrelle
chapters.summary: The wards rise as the stars return; the city wakes to a sky it had stopped believing in, and Ilsa quietly destroys the conscription ledgers. POV Ilsa. Emotional beat: weary, earned relief—justice delivered outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: Empty Hands
chapters.summary: Elodie wakes with no talent left—her gift spent stealing the fire—and must face the city, and Tomas, as simply herself. POV Elodie. Emotional beat: vulnerable rebirth; belonging without bargaining for the first time.

chapters.title: Zephyrine and the Veil
chapters.summary: Months later, Elodie runs a shop selling honest charms—pressed flowers, river stones—beside Tomas, who tends a small warm flame that never goes out. The veil between memory and self, she reflects, was always hers to lift. POV Elodie. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won belonging; the thief who stole nothing in the end.
